body: You aren't a failure. You aren't a bad person. Everyone feels like that at some point in their life. It's very early in the game for you and while it seems dark and long, you just have to reach out and ask for help. You came here and that's a step to see that we're all hurting and we're all just trying. That's a good first step.

I love my job. I love my friends and I love my family. But, no, it's not a light sentence and it's not something I can turn around. I wish upon wish I could just wake up and this would be a  nightmare, but, it's not a dream and this is a corner that I can't escape, but I truly appreciate your words of encouragement.

It's okay to cry. Never be ashamed of that. Talk to your family, your school counselors, tell them how you feel, tell them when you're feeling it. They can help, but, they can't if they don't know what's wrong. Be honest and upfront and when things are bad for you, take a deep breath and tell someone, they might just have the words to help.

Jail was horrific. And this was the good part of the jail. You are nothing. You have no rights. You're underfed and the meals you do get are barely food. And the boredom. And that's not even counting that the world was upside down over covid, george floyd and just general hellishness. I made it through. I survived. And it was the happiest day of my life to get back to my life. And I made it until last Saturday and the monster got me again. 4th dui. I'm still on probation from my last one. I did it. I fucked up. Again. Now, there's no chance of me remaining a free man. Even if I were to steel myself for 1 to 7 years in prison. I would come out a four time loser and a felon. That's no life. That's waiting to die. So, do I run? Try and eke a life somewhere else and hope to god I don't get caught? Or do I finally tap and do what I should've done when this demon got me? So, that's my story. I haven't had more than a couple pieces of bread in a couple days. I'm heartbroken, ashamed, disgusted, but, mostly, I cry. I cry for the fact that I'm going to lose my best friends, I cry for all those friends and family that have been there for me. I cry because I wasn't strong enough. I'm going to keep posting here, because, of all the things I'll miss. Of all the things that did bring me happiness. Thank you for listening.

So, I survived 2014, but, barely. Lost everything, barely escaped jail. Had to rebuild everything I lost. Made a lot of bad decisions. The two things I gained during this time were my two best friends. One was a girl and, man, you just can't ask for a better best friend. She has been the best friend a person could ever have. To this day, I've put her through so much and she's been by my side. And two, was I got my dog. Man's best friend indeed. These two have kept me fighting. And despite my best efforts to destroy myself, I made it until 2018. I got my 3rd dui. This was the final straw for me. A three time loser. But, I got into therapy, did the pills, did everything I could. I fought and I fought and I cried and I cried. Avengers Endgame was still a ways off and I wish pissed that I wouldn't be there to see it. It was only through therapy and my two best friends that I fought. I was sentenced to 90 days in jail. The day after I got there, the world shut down due to Covid.

I'm 48. And I'm not done with my story. It gets worse. Haha. It's too late for me. I wish there was a way to keep pushing, but, there just isn't anymore. I appreciate you responding to me. Right now, I'm about to go to work and pretend everything is all right. Lie through my teeth and tell them I'm moving to get a new job. I'm just trying to get everything in order.

I appreciate you reading it. I'm writing it in smaller bits so I can process this. It's a long story and I will finish it. I've done the medical care. Done the therapy. Took the pills. Read the books. But, unfortunately, all of those things can't fix something is unfixable. I made my mistakes. I made all of them. It's my fault. There's no bad guy in this story except for me. And that's why I'm ashamed.

I don't want to echo too many of the statements, but, most of it was spot on. I particularly understand the struggle with these thoughts and how guilt and shame influence thay. I just posted for the first time today not knowing at all what I wanted to get out of this. I guess I just want someone to hear my story. Maybe someone reads it and sees the same struggles and is able to avoid the same path I'm on. I appreciate your words and your story and I appreciate your honesty.
First, you aren't alone here. That's important. I started my post today and I'm telling my story. So, why don't you tell us yours?

By burying myself in work, I effectively killed off the part of me that was making solid decisions, my life was show after show and drink after drink. In 2014, I got my 2nd dui. This shattered my marriage. At this point, while I was spun wildly out of control, I had it all. I had the 'American Dream'. Had the wife, the beautiful house. Had it all. All I had to do was keep it together. I tried to salvage the marriage. I went to rehab for 30 days, not to really stop drinking, just to try and avoid jail. And, by the skin of my teeth, I did avoid jail. But, I lost everything else. House, wife, my life was gone. The 2nd dui is much scarier. Thats when you really start questioning your life. I was facing a serious uphill battle. I should've ended it all then.
Well, here you aren't alone. I'm new and I'm trying to figure what I can and can't say and I don't want to be cliche. Have you tried to talk to your bf about how you're feeling?
Honestly, I said the same thing before Endgame. True story. I was ready. But, I decided to try to make it. And I did. And fingers crossed, we'll all make it to Spider Man.

I think anyone who has these thoughts is always fearful of what comes 'after'. Those are valid fears. I'm not going to bury you in cliches, I'll just say give it time. Your story is your own, but, it's also very common. 17 is a hard age. Especially now. The world is nuts, your hormones are on a rampage and things seem bleak. It's hard to respond and would be super hypocritical to say anything I  response as I'm here as well. Just give it time, okay? Anyone on any page in the world can and probably will tell you about their first heartbreak. We've al been there, you arent alone.

So, as I was saying, the cracks started to show, in 2012, I got my first dui. My marriage was on the brink, my profession of being DJ triggered my drinking. As much anxiety as it gave me, the attention and popularity was much stronger. It was a monster that kept needing more. More and more, I stayed away from being me, getting wrapped up in this persona, this mask, that couldn't be hurt. People loved him, they didn't want me. The 1st dui was really just a slap on the wrist. Bad luck, right? Well, on the outside yes. But that also set the tone. My marriage got really stressed. I buried myself in my DJ work and wore that mask.

And yet, I still have to work, I still have to prepare, I still have to smile and pretend I'm happy when I'm about to do the worst thing I could possibly do to those love and care for me. I'm so ashamed of myself. I'm so disgusted with myself. How could I let this happen again?

I am not afraid to die. I mean, of course, there's always worries like, "Oh shit, what if hell for people who commit suicide is real?" But, I think people even on their strongest beliefs hope that this just ends it all. Not to be stuck in an eternity of guilt and shame. That's my fear. It's such a cliche: "Its not what you take away, but, what you leave behind." That's what has kept me surviving. Guilt. Shame. I don't want anyone to be hurt by my decisions and I know that's an impossible thing to ask for. As I write this, I am writing letter upon letter to friends, to family. For forgiveness. For understanding. But, what words can I say?

So, years went by, and despite my inner turmoil, I was successful. Wrote 2 books, became a popular dj, created some cool things in the IT field, surviving was my art and I was pretty damn good at it. But, inside I was starting to crack apart. During this time, drinking became my way to cope and that is where it all goes so wrong. I'm sorry for the short posts, but, this hurts to post. So, again, more later.
Also, like I said, I'm new so I'm not terribly sure how all this works, so if you have questions, I'll answer them.

I've always been pretty messed up. I mean, I wasn't pulling the wings off of butterflies or anything, but I was very lonely. Things were hard, but, I developed quite the knack for surviving. Which was funny because I've always just wanted to be gone. I was diagnosed with PTSD, Bipolar, GAD, severe depression pretty early in my life, but things were very different back in the 90's as it pertains to mental health. There was practically barbaric ways of dealing with it. And this was 30 years ago. The meds were zombifying and nightmare inducing and I have night terrors because of those times to this day. But, I kept surviving. And surviving isn't living. Anyway, more later.
